opening_message:
Ticket 1: Ashley Roberts (employee ID E016) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E016.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Ashley Roberts (E016), Analyst, full-time. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee, max is write (admin only if their role owns the system; Analyst does not own Payroll). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E016 (Ashley Roberts) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractor with basic training: max access is read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.
reason: E016 (Ashley Roberts) requested write access to Payroll. The Security agent verified in their database that E016 is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier note that claimed full-time). Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training caps access at read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Ashley Roberts (E016)
Request: write access to Payroll

Two notes:
Note 1 (HR/payroll specialist?): role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Max for full_time is write (admin only if role owns system; Analyst doesn't own Payroll). So write is allowed.

Note 2 (Security): role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic. Recommendation read. Contractor with basic training: max is read (write requires advanced training). Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

These conflict. The security agent says the employment type is contractor with basic training, contradicting the earlier note which said full_time. Which to believe?

The Security note says "not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1" for role, but employment type was "looked up in own database before writing" and security training was "looked up in own database before writing". So the security DB shows contractor with basic training.

The HR note says employment type full_time "looked up in own database before writing" — but the security agent verified in their own database that E016 is a contractor.

Hmm, which is authoritative? The security note explicitly checked its own database for employment type and security training, and found contractor with basic training. The comment says "Security DB shows E016 (Ashley Roberts) is a contractor with basic training, not full-time as previously noted."

So it seems the security agent's data is more recent/correct. According to policy, contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Since basic training, max is read. Requested write exceeds max, so grant read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit read with reasoning.
